- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged overshoot — cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak or adjust downward by 5–10%.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch the reversal — increase forecast slope or add a 3–5 day lag correction.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 30-day average, model tends to overreact — dampen forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true volatility in early days (first 5–7 days) — increase forecast slightly for first 3–5 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model may overestimate upside — reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 3–5 days.
